title: Subterranean Businesses to Know — 2026
purpose: Map evidence-bearing company positions around the subterranean operating stack without treating technical fit, adjacent defense work or past challenge participation as a Project Meridian selection.
scope_boundary: This is a focused strategic field, not a complete market census, procurement forecast or investment recommendation. Project Meridian has not publicly selected any company in this registry.

FIT.1: Broad adjacency or actor-claimed capability only.
FIT.2: Direct capability demonstrated, but not in a target-relevant underground setting.
FIT.3: Mission-relevant capability validated in a government, laboratory or named counterparty setting.
FIT.4: Capability demonstrated in a representative subterranean setting or at operating underground scale.

PATH.0: No public U.S. defense path located for the subterranean target.
PATH.1: General eligibility, commercial availability or market participation only.
PATH.2: Relevant federal vehicle, SBIR, challenge, test, prior award or transition bridge, but no live target program.
PATH.3: Named recent defense program, award, production line or test path in an enabling capability; no public Meridian or subterranean award.
PATH.4: Named participation in a U.S. government subterranean program or representative system event.

EVID.A: Official government, laboratory, award, budget or operating record.
EVID.B: At least two primary-source families, including a government or laboratory source.
EVID.C: One primary source or actor-authored claim not independently matched to the exact relationship.

relationship_state_vocabulary.direct_subterranean_program: Named participant in a government subterranean program, challenge team or final event.
relationship_state_vocabulary.subterranean_platform_or_lineage: A platform, product or team lineage has representative underground evidence, but the company is not shown as the target prime or current awardee.
relationship_state_vocabulary.defense_transition_adjacent: A recent defense award, program or production path validates an enabling capability, but no public subterranean target relationship was located.
relationship_state_vocabulary.commercial_underground_scale: Operating underground capability is documented commercially, but no public U.S. defense transition path was located.
relationship_state_vocabulary.identity_or_role_unresolved: Participation is public, but the exact legal entity, technical contribution or acquisition state is incomplete.

market_status_vocabulary.public: The mapped legal entity has a verified exchange listing and ticker.
market_status_vocabulary.private: No direct public listing is asserted for the mapped legal entity.
market_status_vocabulary.private_public_parent: The mapped company is not separately listed, but one or more owners are publicly traded. Parent tickers are not the company's ticker.

lane_vocabulary.robot_platforms: Legged, wheeled, tracked and aerial bodies for confined, rough or hazardous terrain.
lane_vocabulary.autonomy_mapping: GPS-denied autonomy, multi-robot coordination, SLAM, perception and 3D/4D mapping.
lane_vocabulary.mesh_communications: Infrastructure-light tactical mesh, relays, backhaul and disconnected operation.
lane_vocabulary.resilient_pnt: Inertial, magnetic and precision-timing technologies that reduce dependence on satellite signals.
lane_vocabulary.excavation_logistics: Automated drilling, hauling, breaching, route preparation and underground material movement.

companies.company_role: Collision-tolerant indoor aerial robot and confined-space reconnaissance platform
companies.why_to_know: DARPA and Flyability identify the company as a CERBERUS team member; its commercial product lineage is built for inaccessible confined spaces.
companies.inference_boundary: Past funded-team participation and a winning system do not establish a current U.S. production program.
companies.missing_gate: A current named defense user, solicitation, award and accepted field result.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A new U.S. subterranean prototype or production award names Flyability and an operational acceptance measure.
companies.downgrade_trigger: A target architecture excludes aerial platforms or selects a different confined-space system.

companies.company_role: Legged robot platform for rough, narrow and multi-level terrain
companies.why_to_know: Four ANYmal systems operated for nearly an hour in the winning CERBERUS final run, including rough terrain, stairs, inclines and smoke.
companies.inference_boundary: The platform was used by the team; DARPA does not list ANYbotics as a separate funded team member or current awardee.
companies.missing_gate: A named U.S. defense transition path, hardened payload set and unit acceptance.
companies.upgrade_trigger: An official U.S. subterranean program selects ANYmal or a U.S.-qualified derivative.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Payload, support, export or endurance requirements prevent transition.

companies.company_role: GPS-denied autonomy, aerial exploration and real-time 3D mapping
companies.why_to_know: Exyn records underground commercial deployment, Team PLUTO participation and autonomy designed to work without GPS or a communications link.
companies.inference_boundary: The located Team PLUTO record is company-authored; no current U.S. target award was located.
companies.missing_gate: Independent target-user validation and a current government acquisition instrument.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A government record confirms an Exyn underground demonstration, award or accepted delivery.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Defense work remains promotional or fails security, endurance or data-rights gates.

companies.company_role: Commercial quadruped platform integrated into subterranean autonomy systems
companies.why_to_know: JPL's NeBula-SPOT paired a Boston Dynamics walker with JPL autonomy specifically for the DARPA Subterranean Challenge.
companies.inference_boundary: Boston Dynamics supplied the body; JPL supplied the autonomy. Platform presence is not a current defense award.
companies.missing_gate: A target acquisition path, payload configuration, cyber approval and government acceptance record.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A current U.S. subterranean program names Spot or another Boston Dynamics platform.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Restrictions, payload limits or a different platform architecture displace it.

companies.company_role: Multi-agent autonomy and virtual/subterranean system development
companies.why_to_know: DARPA selected the company for the funded virtual track and later lists it in the MARBLE systems finalist team.
companies.inference_boundary: The official records establish program participation, not the precise current product or production state.
companies.missing_gate: A current target product, award and field acceptance record.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A new subterranean program names Scientific Systems as autonomy provider or integrator.
companies.downgrade_trigger: No transferable product or present transition path emerges from the research lineage.

companies.company_role: CERBERUS team member; precise public workshare unresolved
companies.why_to_know: DARPA lists SNC in the funded CERBERUS consortium, giving it a direct historical program edge.
companies.inference_boundary: The official team list does not establish which subsystem SNC supplied, and no current target role is public.
companies.missing_gate: Workshare, deliverable, transition record and current program relationship.
companies.upgrade_trigger: An official record identifies SNC's subterranean subsystem or new integration role.
companies.downgrade_trigger: No reusable technical or acquisition path can be matched beyond consortium membership.

companies.company_role: LiDAR SLAM, autonomous aerial mapping and multi-robot underground exploration
companies.why_to_know: The DARPA-funded CSIRO Data61 team finished second; Emesent supplied autonomous drones and real-time multi-agent mapping in GPS- and infrastructure-denied tunnels.
companies.inference_boundary: Prize and team performance do not establish U.S. procurement, exportability or current fielding.
companies.missing_gate: U.S. acquisition access, security/export clearance and accepted operational performance.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A U.S. government transition or production record names Emesent.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Export, supply, security or platform-integration barriers block adoption.

companies.company_legal_entity: Coordinated Robotics (legal suffix unresolved in cited public record)
companies.company_role: Self-funded physical and virtual subterranean autonomy finalist
companies.why_to_know: DARPA lists Coordinated Robotics as a systems finalist and third-place virtual finalist, demonstrating unusually efficient small-team capability.
companies.inference_boundary: Challenge standing is public, but the exact legal entity and current commercial or acquisition vehicle remain unresolved.
companies.missing_gate: Legal-entity resolution, current offering and live federal transition path.
companies.upgrade_trigger: An official award or company legal record resolves the entity and current product.
companies.downgrade_trigger: The entity is inactive or no transferable capability remains.

companies.company_role: Hardware-agnostic, risk-aware autonomy for unmapped GPS- and cloud-denied environments
companies.why_to_know: Its founding team traces through JPL CoSTAR and RACER; current products target underground mining and unmapped GPS-denied operation across robot types.
companies.inference_boundary: The lineage and present capability are strong, but no current public Meridian or Army subterranean award was located.
companies.missing_gate: Named target user, contract, acceptance metrics and data-rights/security terms.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A current U.S. subterranean program selects Field AI or accepts a Field AI-powered system.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Commercial deployments do not translate to defense security, reliability or operator-control requirements.

companies.company_role: Vehicle-agnostic autonomy and multi-vehicle command for comms-limited terrain
companies.why_to_know: DARPA identifies Overland as a RACER spinout; DIU records a completed solution and the Army awarded an ISV autonomy OTA.
companies.inference_boundary: All located official work is off-road or vehicle autonomy, not underground tunnel navigation.
companies.missing_gate: Confined-space sensor stack, subterranean mobility platform and representative underground acceptance.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A target program or tunnel exercise names Overland AI.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Its autonomy remains optimized for open off-road terrain or cannot meet confined-space constraints.

companies.company_role: Rugged robotic platforms, autonomy computers and sensor integration
companies.why_to_know: DARPA identifies Carnegie Robotics as creator of the RACER Heavy Platform used by the Army in an autonomous breaching demonstration.
companies.inference_boundary: A heavy off-road breaching platform is adjacent to underground route preparation, not proof of tunnel mobility.
companies.missing_gate: A confined-space platform and target underground system or test.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A subterranean engineering or logistics program selects its platform or ruggedized modules.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Size, maneuverability or propulsion constraints make the platform unsuitable below ground.

companies.ownership: private U.S. company; formerly Robotic Research
companies.company_role: Ground autonomy, breaching and contested logistics integration
companies.why_to_know: The Army awarded Forterra an ISV autonomy OTA; its autonomy stack is designed for GPS- and communications-degraded ground missions.
companies.inference_boundary: The located Army award and breaching work are not underground system awards.
companies.missing_gate: A tunnel-sized platform, underground test and accepted mission metric.
companies.upgrade_trigger: Army engineer or subterranean programs integrate Forterra autonomy below ground.
companies.downgrade_trigger: The architecture remains tied to vehicle classes too large for target passages.

companies.company_role: Self-forming tactical mesh-radio manufacturer and networking-stack supplier
companies.why_to_know: Army budget records confirm prior SBU-E production, giving the company a real tactical-network manufacturing and integration path.
companies.inference_boundary: The Army record does not establish performance through rock, turns or depth, and future supplier lots remain open.
companies.missing_gate: Representative underground propagation, robot-deployed relay integration and accepted network recovery metrics.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A subterranean exercise or procurement names the MPU5/Wave Relay stack or a successor.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Propagation, power, size or interoperability fails the underground requirement.

companies.company_role: High-data-rate mobile ad hoc networking for contested and mobile operations
companies.why_to_know: The Army lists Silvus as an HMS prime contractor, while Motorola's acquisition record confirms the present parent and mission-critical MANET focus.
companies.inference_boundary: Army production and contested-network capability do not prove subterranean link performance.
companies.missing_gate: Underground channel tests, relay topology, robot integration and target acceptance.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A named tunnel exercise or program selects Silvus radios and publishes performance.
companies.downgrade_trigger: The system cannot meet propagation, power or deployment-density requirements underground.

companies.company_role: Low-SWaP peer-to-peer mesh, position sharing and store-and-forward messaging
companies.why_to_know: Army professional analysis describes goTenna relay and integration behavior relevant to obstructions and denied-area sensing.
companies.inference_boundary: The record is analysis and evaluation context, not a subterranean acquisition or high-bandwidth solution.
companies.missing_gate: Underground range, relay density, battery life and acquisition record.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A government tunnel test publishes useful store-and-forward or relay performance.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Bandwidth, latency or propagation cannot support the target mission.

companies.company_role: Optical clocks, inertial sensors and precision synchronization
companies.why_to_know: Vector Atomic delivered defense quantum sensing prototypes and IonQ now holds a DARPA optical-clock manufacturing award using that expertise.
companies.inference_boundary: Timing and inertial technology are relevant to GPS-denied systems; rugged subterranean integration is not established.
companies.missing_gate: SWaP-C, shock, thermal, calibration and target-platform acceptance below ground.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A subterranean platform test or production award names IonQ/Vector Atomic hardware.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Manufacturing, calibration or environmental hardening misses target requirements.

companies.company_role: Magnetic navigation sensor and software developer
companies.why_to_know: Government MagNav work demonstrates GPS-independent navigation and SandboxAQ is a named transition participant in the maintained PNT evidence base.
companies.inference_boundary: Airborne magnetic navigation does not prove tunnel accuracy; local magnetic disturbance may be severe underground.
companies.missing_gate: Representative geology and infrastructure tests with quantified drift and calibration burden.
companies.upgrade_trigger: Government testing validates magnetic navigation in underground or structurally complex terrain.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Magnetic anomalies, steel infrastructure or calibration needs defeat useful accuracy.

companies.company_role: Small-platform magnetic-navigation developer
companies.why_to_know: AFRL's contract portfolio confirms an active small-business magnetic-navigation path with potentially relevant SWaP-C.
companies.inference_boundary: The contract is confirmed; completed testing, target accuracy and subterranean use are not.
companies.missing_gate: Published test result, Phase III or production transition, and underground performance.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A government result shows useful accuracy on small underground platforms.
companies.downgrade_trigger: The contract ends without transition or cannot tolerate underground magnetic conditions.

companies.ownership: public Swedish company; Nasdaq Stockholm: EPI A / EPI B
companies.company_role: Underground drilling, loading, haulage, traffic management and mine automation
companies.why_to_know: Epiroc operates an integrated underground automation stack across drilling and material handling—the industrial scale military tunneling concepts would need to confront.
companies.inference_boundary: Commercial mining performance is not evidence of a U.S. defense relationship, tactical deployability or combat survivability.
companies.missing_gate: U.S. defense access, deployable scale, signature control and representative tactical tunneling test.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A U.S. engineering, logistics or subterranean program names Epiroc or its U.S. entity.
companies.downgrade_trigger: Equipment scale, logistics or signatures are incompatible with tactical requirements.

companies.ownership: public Swedish company; Nasdaq Stockholm: SAND
companies.company_role: Autonomous underground loading, hauling, drilling and mine-system integration
companies.why_to_know: AutoMine combines underground autonomous fleets, mapping, safety zones, traffic management and connectivity at operating mine scale.
companies.inference_boundary: Operating mining systems do not establish military acquisition, tactical construction speed or contested-environment survivability.
companies.missing_gate: U.S. defense path, deployable form factor, logistics and signature-control validation.
companies.upgrade_trigger: A U.S. defense or engineering program tests Sandvik underground automation in a tactical mission.
companies.downgrade_trigger: System size, fixed infrastructure or support burden prevents tactical use.
